newsitem.title: UK: Defence project delays cost Britain dear - report.
newsitem.headline: Defence project delays cost Britain dear - report.

text.p: Britain's Ministry of Defence is running 1.3 billion pounds ($2.1 billion) over budget on major projects and on average some three years late, the Financial Times on Friday quoted a National Audit Office (NAO) report as saying.
The NAO said procurement was so behind schedule that outdated ships, tanks and aircraft were being repaired at a cost of 400 million pounds.
It found an increase in projected costs for 23 projects of 1.37 billion pounds, an 8.7 percent overshoot, the Financial Times said.
The most common reason for cost overshoots was changes to the nature or scope of projects.
The Ministry of Defence said it was "vigorously examining" equipment procurement practices, the Press Association news agency reported. ($ = 0.630 British Pounds)
